name: Forearm Plank
instructions: Rest on forearms with elbows directly under shoulders.
Step feet back and extend legs, maintaining a straight line from heels to head.
Squeeze glutes and draw navel in towards spine.
Hold steadily without allowing hips to drop or rise.
commonMistakes: Hips sagging towards the floor (compresses lumbar spine)
coachTips: Actively pull your elbows toward your toes to engage the deep transverse core.
breathingTip: Breathe steadily in through nose, out through mouth; don't hold breath.
progressionNote: Build up to a 60-second solid hold before adding movements.

name: Dead Bug (Back Friendly Core)
targetMuscles: Deep Core & Anterior Pelvic Tilt Correction
instructions: Lie flat on back with arms pointing to ceiling and knees bent at 90 degrees.
Press lower back completely flat against the floor.
Simultaneously lower right arm and left leg until hovering above floor.
Return to center and switch sides.
commonMistakes: Allowing lower back to arch off the floor
coachTips: The golden rule: if your lower back peels off the floor, shorten your leg reach.
breathingTip: Exhale as limbs extend; inhale returning to center.
progressionNote: Hold a resistance band for increased anti-extension tension.

name: Bird-Dog (Spine Health)
instructions: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.
Extend right arm forward and left leg backward until parallel to floor.
Hold for 2 seconds keeping hips square to floor.
Return to hands and knees and repeat on opposite side.
commonMistakes: Rotating hips and flaring the extending leg wide
coachTips: Part of the famous McGill Big 3 for bulletproofing the lower back.
breathingTip: Inhale to center; exhale as arm and leg reach out.
progressionNote: Square hips so a cup of water could rest on your lower back.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with arms extended.
Without swinging, curl knees or straight legs upward toward chest.
Tilt pelvis upward at the top to fully engage the abs.
Lower slowly with control.
commonMistakes: Swinging body to kick legs up
coachTips: Tuck knees to chest first if straight legs cause swinging.
breathingTip: Exhale bringing legs up; inhale lowering down.
progressionNote: Progress from knee raises to toes-to-bar.

name: Side Plank
instructions: Lie on your side with forearm flat on ground beneath shoulder.
Stack feet and lift hips off the floor into a straight diagonal line.
Hold position, keeping neck neutral and glutes engaged.
coachTips: Drive bottom hip upward to activate the lateral core.
breathingTip: Steady calm breathing throughout the hold.
progressionNote: Raise top leg for an elevated star side plank.

name: Cable Woodchoppers
instructions: Set cable high. Stand sideways to the machine gripping handle with both hands.
Rotate torso downward and diagonally across your body to outside opposite knee.
Pivot on back foot, control rotation back to start.
commonMistakes: Pulling only with arms instead of rotating through core
coachTips: Pivot back foot like squishing a bug to keep knees safe during rotation.
progressionNote: Perform both high-to-low and low-to-high variations.

name: Bicycle Crunches
instructions: Lie on back with fingertips lightly touching ears, knees bent at 90 degrees.
Bring right elbow to left knee while extending right leg out straight.
Switch sides in a smooth pedaling motion.
coachTips: Think of bringing shoulder to knee, not just elbow.
breathingTip: Rhythmic exhale as you twist to each side.
progressionNote: Slow tempo (2 seconds per twist) triples core activation.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Kneel on a soft mat holding ab wheel with both hands under shoulders.
Tuck pelvis and round upper back slightly.
Roll wheel forward as far as comfortable without lower back collapsing.
Contract abs to pull wheel back to starting position.
commonMistakes: Lower back arching into hyperextension at full extension
coachTips: Only roll out as far as you can maintain a hollow rock pelvic tilt.
breathingTip: Inhale rolling out; exhale contracting back.
progressionNote: Roll out to a wall boundary to control depth.
